name: MediaRecorder
plain: Records a camera, mic or screen stream to a file in the page.
meaning: Turns a live stream into stored audio or video. Needs a stream the person already allowed; the point is the site can keep a copy, upload it, or hold it in memory.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt of its own; permission comes from the source stream.
access.revocation: Stop the tracks or stop the recorder

data.update: every timeslice ms (default 0, one blob at stop)

limits.headline: Can save a camera, mic or screen stream to a file, once you allowed it
limits.user_action: You click Record on a page that already has camera, mic or screen access
can: Record video or audio from a stream you already allowed
Save the recording in the page and offer it to download
Upload the recording to the site's servers
Stop and start recording while the tab stays open
cannot: Record anything without an allowed camera, mic or screen share first
Record sources you did not allow
Show its own prompt; the only prompt is for the camera, mic or screen
Keep recording once the source stops or the tab closes

story.what_it_is: Lets a page record a live camera, mic or screen stream and keep it as a file.

marketing.name: MediaRecorder
marketing.pitch: Developer docs show how a page can record audio or video streams into chunks and save or upload them.

story.for_you: You do not see a prompt for this itself. It only works on a stream you already allowed, such as your camera. If the site records, you may see a red dot or a Recording note, but it is not required.
story.for_makers: Recording turns a live moment into a product: a saved message, a replay, an upload for later review. It also lets a maker keep a copy of calls for training and compliance. Because it runs in the browser, there is no extra app to build or ship.

use_cases.example: In Loom or a similar tool, you press Record, speak and share your tab, and the page saves it as a video file you can send.
A voice note button in a web chat records your voice from the mic and sends it as a short audio clip.
A browser game lets you press a key to record your last 30 seconds of play, and the page makes a clip to share.
A language app records you saying a phrase, then plays it back next to the native speaker so you can compare.
A sales call site records the call in the browser and uploads it for coaching, when the host turns recording on.
A video ID check records a short selfie clip and sends it to a server to confirm you are a live person.
A podcast tool records your mic locally at high quality, then uploads the file after the show, so a bad connection does not ruin it.

risks: Copy of a call kept without everyone's knowledge
Recordings stored on a vendor server
